title: Ethiopian Easter Sweet (Fasika)
community: Ethiopian Orthodox Christians — the Easter (Fasika) celebration sweet
author: Mama Tigist
desc: Ethiopian Easter Sweet Bread — a small, individual-sized Difo Dabo (ETH004) made for Easter morning. Each person receives their own small bread loaf after the 55-day Lenten fast, marked with a cross and glazed with honey. The most emotionally significant sweet in Ethiopian Orthodox life.
longDesc: The Fasika sweet bread is the most anticipated food in Ethiopian Orthodox Christianity — made in individual portions (one per family member), baked on Easter Saturday, and distributed after the midnight Easter service. After 55 days of fasting, each person holds their own small cross-marked honey bread.
ingredients: // Individual-sized Difo Dabo — make per ETH004 recipe
// Scale to make 16 small individual loaves (instead of one large)
// Each marked with a deep cross
// Each glazed with Ethiopian honey immediately out of the oven
equipment: Individual muffin tins or shape by hand
steps: Make Difo Dabo dough per ETH004.
Shape each into a small round loaf.
Score a deep cross into the top of each.
Serve to each person individually at the Easter feast.
chefTips: Individual size is the point — each person receives their own.
The cross marking is sacred — deep and clear.
Honey glaze immediately out of the oven — while still hot.
servedWith: Distributed at the Easter morning feast after 55-day Lent
healthBenefits: Fenugreek supports recovery after 55-day fasting period.
culturalNote: The Fasika small bread is the most emotionally powerful food in Ethiopian Orthodox Christianity — the individual bread given to each person after 55 days of fasting, marked with the cross, glazed with honey. When the family gathers at Easter dawn and each person holds their own honey-glazed bread, the joy is not just about food — it is about endurance, faith, and community.
